title: SF2959 (2017-2018 Regular): Semiautomatic military-style assault weapon minimum age to possess raised; semiautomatic military-style assault weapon definition expansion; semiautomatic military-style assault weapon transfer to underage persons crime

provenance.fetched_by: Open States bulk data (Minnesota) (gun-policy Stage 5, Minnesota); operative text read by a Sonnet fill agent from the official Minnesota text (Introduction; official copy, https://www.revisor.mn.gov/bills/90/2018/0/SF/2959/versions/0/)
provenance.note: Introduced version as filed (SF 2959, 2017-2018 session). Struck words are not quoted: the old age 18 in 624.713 and 'or semiautomatic military-style assault weapon' in the transfer felony (Section 5). The (ii) quote leaves out a struck 'and'. The bill also raises the age to 21 for the assault-weapon rules in Section 4(1) and expands the definition of the weapon in Section 1.

Section 2 (Minn. Stat. 624.712, new subd. 13): "Detachable magazine" means an ammunition feeding device that can be loaded or unloaded while detached from a firearm and readily inserted into a firearm.
Section 1 (Minn. Stat. 624.712, subd. 7): (2) semiautomatic pistol, or any semiautomatic, centerfire, or rimfire rifle with a fixed magazine, that has the capacity to accept more than seven rounds of ammunition;
Section 4 (Minn. Stat. 624.713, subd. 1): (ii) a person under the age of 21 years may possess ammunition designed for use in a firearm that the person may lawfully possess; (iv) a person under the age of 21 years may carry or possess a semiautomatic military-style assault weapon:
